newsitem.title: CHINA: China firms win $807 mln contracts on Three Gorges.
newsitem.headline: China firms win $807 mln contracts on Three Gorges.

text.p: Three Chinese companies have won $807 million worth of contracts for the construction and installation of dam and power plant workshops for the huge Three Gorges dam, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

The three companies are Gezhouba Share Holding Ltd, Yichang Qingyun Hydropower Joint Management Co and Yichang Three Gorges Project Construction 378 Joint Management, it said without giving details of the size of the various contracts.
The three companies will be responsible for building a flood discharge dike, ground workshops and power plant workshops and dikes on the left bank, it said.

This second phase is the most difficult and largest section of the Three Gorges dam project, the world's largest water control project, it quoted Lu Youmei, president of the China Yangtze Three Gorges Project Development Corp, as saying.

The construction work will involve excavation of approximately eight million cubic metres of earth and stone and the pouring of 12.4 million cubic metres of concrete as well as the installation of 148,700 tonnes of equipment and metal structures, he said.

The first phase of the project, launched in 1993, involves damming the Yangtze river in November. The second phase will last six years and involves building the reservoir and setting up power generation.
The whole project is due for completion by 2009 and is expected to cost about 200 billion yuan ($24.1 billion). It will flood 28,000 hectares of farmland and displace 1.13 million people.
Project officials said last Friday they would decide the winner of a tender to supply generators for the dam in the next few days.
Officials declined to give details of the prospects of any of the groups bidding to supply 14 generating units for the world's biggest water project.

Officials had named the groups in the running for the contract as including Siemens AG and GE Canada; Anglo-French group GEC Alsthom; Swedish-Swiss ABB ; a Russian consortium; a Japanese group; and Impsa of Argentina as well as Westinghouse Canada.
